In summary, our research is concerned with
a new and potentially important aspect of LN function and may have implications in the pathogenesis of neoplastic diseases.

the identification of the LN isoforms that are involved in the extravasating process and with the characterization of the LN receptor molecules mediating the interaction of extravascular cells with the subendothelium.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LNs are the primary components of the vascular basement membrane that promote the interaction with neoplasia lymphocytes and that this interaction is mediated by integrins alpha3beta1 or alpha6beta1.

LN-8 is a primary LN component of the endothelial subbasement membrane favoring the extravasation and/or the survival of neoplastic and normal B cells, and LN- 10 is a primary component of the subendotheial basement membrane favoring extravasation of T cells.
the LN isoforms 8 (LN-8) and 10 (LN-10) are the major components of the endothelium basement membrane promoting interaction of neoplastic cells of lymphoid origin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LN-8, LN-10, or a combination of the two may be implicated as a molecular marker for the detection and monitoring of lymphoma and leukemia.
LNs may be considered as a new family of endothelial adhesion molecules.

the subendothelium is a dynamic and complex environment, where different isoforms of the same protein family may be involved in the regulation of cell migration, differentiation, and survival, thus contributing to the establishment and maintenance of the vascular microenvironment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of LN-specific antibodies may be of great utility in identifying the LN isoforms that are preferentially expressed in the vascular structures involved in the extravasations of different cell types.
the LN isoforms 8, 9, and 10 are likely candidates for targeting in the treatment of neoplastic disorders.
LN-8, LN-10, or a mixture thereof may be considered as potential targets for therapeutic intervention aimed at preventing lymphoma cell dissemination.
